title: Smooth fibre point admits an etale immersion slice
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a smooth morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $x\in X$ map to $s\in S$, assume $x$ is closed in the fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and assume $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$ is finite (finite-dimensional as a vector space) and separable algebraic [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Then there exist a scheme $Z$, an immersion $i:Z\to X$ (a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]), and $z\in Z$ with $i(z)=x$, such that $Z\to S$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] and the scheme-theoretic fibre $Z_s$ has underlying set $\{z\}$.

source.place: Tag 057G, lemma-slice-smooth, including the immersion conclusion and Z_s={x} set-theoretically

proof.text: Smoothness includes local finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], so by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] there are affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\ni x$ of $X$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\ni s$ of $S$ with $f(W)\subset V$ and $A$ finitely presented over $R$. Apply [lem-trf-affine-fibre-point-dimension] to this chart: $\dim_x(X_s)=\dim_{\mathfrak Q}(\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(s)\otimes_RA))$ is a finite nonnegative integer $d$. Prove the assertion by strong induction on $d$, simultaneously for every smooth morphism and every closed fibre point with finite separable residue extension. The induction hypothesis includes the immersion, etaleness over the same base, and the singleton designated fibre for every smaller dimension.

source.place: Tag 057G, lemma-slice-smooth, proof, affine reduction and induction on d; finiteness and induction quantifiers expanded

proof.text: If $d=0$, apply [lem-trf-smooth-zero-dimensional-singleton-open] with $W=X$. Its open subscheme $Z$ contains $x$, is etale over $S$, has singleton fibre over $s$, and its inclusion into $X$ is an immersion. Taking $z=x$ gives all the required conclusions.

source.place: Tag 057G, lemma-slice-smooth, proof, d=0 paragraph; singleton fibre by the subspace topology (Schemes Tag 01K1)

proof.text: If $d>0$, [lem-trf-smooth-separable-hypersurface-slice] gives an affine open $U\subseteq X$ and an effective Cartier divisor $D\hookrightarrow U$ through $x$, smooth over $S$, with $\dim_{x_D}(D_s)=d-1$. Here $D_s=D\times_U U_s$ by the fibre-product universal property, so $D_s\to U_s$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). The closed singleton of $X_s$ restricts to the closed singleton $\{x\}$ in $U_s$. Its inverse image is $\{x_D\}$ because a closed immersion is a homeomorphism onto its image [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $x_D$ is closed in $D_s$. The induced residue maps for $D\hookrightarrow U\hookrightarrow X$ are isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-residue-field-iso] and [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality], respectively. Write $a:D\to U$, $b:U\to X$ and $r_h$ for the residue map induced by a morphism $h$. The definition via local stalk maps [def-weil-residue-field] gives $r_{f\circ b\circ a}=r_a\circ r_b\circ r_f$, since stalk maps and their quotient maps compose. Thus the isomorphism $r_a\circ r_b:\kappa(x)\to\kappa(x_D)$ respects the given $\kappa(s)$-algebra structures. Hence the extension at $x_D$ is finite separable. The smooth morphism $D\to S$ and $x_D$ therefore satisfy the induction claim's input hypotheses at dimension $d-1$.

source.place: Tag 057G, lemma-slice-smooth, proof, positive-dimensional slicing and verification of the induction hypotheses

proof.text: Apply the induction hypothesis to $D\to S$ at $x_D$, since $d-1<d$, obtaining $j:Z\to D$ and $z\in Z$. The map $D\hookrightarrow U\hookrightarrow X$ is an immersion by its closed-then-open factorization [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its composite with $j$ is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e), and sends $z$ to $x$. All maps are over $S$, so the structural map of $Z$ and its fibre over $s$ are exactly those supplied by induction. They are etale and the singleton $\{z\}$, respectively. This closes the induction.

source.place: Tag 057G, lemma-slice-smooth, proof, final two sentences: induction on D and composition of the immersions

lean.statement: theorem Smooth.exists_etale_immersion_slice {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Smooth f] (x : X) (hx : IsClosed {f.asFiber x}) (h : @Module.Finite (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x) _ _ (@Algebra.toModule _ _ _ _ (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra) ∧ @Algebra.IsSeparable (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x) _ _ (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra) : ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) (z : Z), IsImmersion i ∧ i z = x ∧ Etale (i ≫ f) ∧ Set.range ((i ≫ f).fiberι (f x)) = Set.singleton z
